methods.label: Identify what would make the claim false
methods.explanation: The conjecture says that every even integer greater than \(2\) has a representation as a sum of two primes. To disprove it, one would need an even integer greater than \(2\) for which no such representation exists. Odd integers are outside the claim, and a decomposition into nonprimes does not rule out a different decomposition into primes. Thus a counterexample would be an even integer greater than \(2\) that cannot be written as the sum of two prime numbers, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses the elementary meaning of a counterexample to an every-number claim.
